Predicting degradation in direct ammonia SOFCs: The temperature trade–off between nickel nitriding and coarsening
items.samenvatting_bron: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free fuel for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), since nickel-based anodes can crack it internally without a separate reformer. Direct-ammonia operation, however, compromises durability through nickel nitriding and coarsening. These mechanisms respond oppositely to temperature and are usually studied separately, leading to conflicting set-point guidance. This study combines both mechanisms in a reduced-order model linking operating conditions to voltage losses. The combined response reveals two effects. First, nitriding is non-monotonic, peaking at approximately 625–665 °C under the assumed kinetics; thus, a moderate increase above 600 °C may accelerate it. Second, the mechanisms cross over at 731–741 °C, with nitriding dominating below and coarsening above. From a degradation perspective, a balanced long-term window of approximately 750–780 °C is identified. Both the crossover and the high-temperature penalty remain robust in a sensitivity analysis. The joint model supports what-if analysis and remaining-useful-life estimation for maintenance planning.

items.titel: Judicial review of bottom‐trawling restrictions in EU marine protected areas: Case T‐265/23 VDK v Commission
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract This case note analyses the EU General Court's judgment in VDK v Commission (Judgment of 21 May 2025, Case T‐265/23), which concerns the legality of spatial fisheries restrictions adopted to protect marine Natura 2000 sites in the German Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). As the applicant did not appeal the judgment, it has become final. The applicant, a German fishers' association, challenged the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/340, which closed four sites in Germany's North Sea EEZ (in addition to three Dutch sites) to bottom‐contacting gear and to gillnets and entangling nets. The applicant argued that the measure was, insofar as it concerned the German sites, disproportionate and that the European Commission exceeded its powers under the Common Fisheries Policy (CFP). The Court dismissed both pleas. First, it reaffirmed the broad discretion enjoyed by European Union (EU) institutions in the field of the CFP, applying a deferential standard of judicial review and endorsing a precautionary approach to bottom‐contacting fishing gear in marine protected areas. Second, it confirmed the Commission's competence to protect gravel beds under Article 11(2) CFP‐Regulation in conjunction with Article 13(4) MSFD. The judgment strengthens the legal resilience of spatial fisheries restrictions used to implement EU biodiversity law, such as the Birds and Habitats Directives. items.titel: Land use occupation and construction around the Córdoba, Capellanía and El Tunjo wetland reserves 1998–2024
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban wetlands (UW) are highly valued ecosystems due to the wide range of services they provide to cities and regions worldwide. They contribute to improved urban air and water quality, enhance human well-being, and play a crucial role in sustainable urban development and climate change mitigation by safeguarding biodiversity, regulating hydrological cycles, and acting as carbon sinks. However, urban growth and consolidation continue to be a major driver of UW degradation, leading towards area decrease, pollution, habitat fragmentation, and loss of biodiversity through infrastructure development, land conversion, and increase of resources demands. In this context, information about existing interactions between city development and UW conservation is essential to explore integrative approaches that enable the protection of urban and peri-urban ecosystems. The present study analyzes land-use occupation and urban development attributes in the surroundings of three UW in Bogotá, Colombia, between 1998 and 2024. Land-use area, together with indices of building coverage (BCI) and floor space (FSI), were comparatively examined within 500-m buffer areas around the Capellanía, Córdoba, and El Tunjo wetland reserves.
